f1.quote: The DLP-printed green bodies were debound under either oxygen-rich ambient air or an oxygen-deficient environment maintained by continuous mechanical-pump evacuation

f2.quote: Debinding included 1 h holds at 300 and 450 °C followed by heating to 500 °C.

f3.quote: then solid-state sintered at 800, 1000, 1050, or 1100 °C for 24 h.

f4.quote: Specimens were printed with a 405 nm source at 19.57 mW/cm², 100 s exposure, 70 μm layers, and 20 layers

f5.quote: Oxygen-deficient debinding retained carbon in former resin regions, reduced pore volume, limited cracking, and permitted earlier loss of the layered morphology and stronger interparticle bonding.

f6.quote: In oxygen-rich debinding, oxidation of resin and powder generates rapidly escaping CO/CO2, causing pressure-driven surface cracking

f7.quote: surface oxides subsequently resist interparticle mass transport and delay densification

f9.quote: Oxygen-deficient debinding retained carbon in former resin regions, reduced pore volume, limited cracking, and permitted earlier loss of the layered morphology

f10.quote: Relative to oxygen-rich debinding, oxygen-deficient debinding is reported to produce earlier densification and comparable maximum compressive strength at a 50 °C lower sintering temperature
